items.title: 南海：菲律宾周边军演与中国海军活动叠加
items.description: 南海方向出现新的军事活动信号。WIRE 信息显示，在“肩并肩”联合军演背景下，中国海军在菲律宾附近海域的部署受到关注。对中国周边安全来说，这类动态的敏感点不在单次行动，而在军事存在、演训频率和外部力量介入是否持续上升。
items.rawSummary: Mayon Volcano remains under Alert Level 3 following a massive eruption, with ongoing ashfall darkening nearby towns and 32 earthquakes reported as activity persists.
items.analysis: A massive eruption occurred at Mayon Volcano on May 2, with Alert Level 3 maintained due to heightened risk. A lava flow collapse triggered a pyroclastic density current, sending ash plumes visible from Legazpi City and raising concerns over air quality, transport, and agriculture in Albay. In the following days, heavy ashfall plunged nearby towns into darkness and 32 earthquakes were reported, signaling continuing unrest. No immediate reports of casualties or evacuation orders have been confirmed.

keyPoints.point: A massive eruption occurred at Mayon Volcano; Alert Level 3 remains in effect.
A lava flow collapse generated a fast-moving pyroclastic density current, with ash plumes visible from Legazpi City and concerns over air quality, transport, and agriculture in Albay.
Ashfall from Mayon Volcano caused darkness in Philippine towns, and 32 earthquakes were reported.

items.title: 北京外交：零关税、台湾议题与对日摩擦同时推进
items.description: 中国相关动态今天集中在外交和经贸层面。WIRE 信息显示，中国对 53 个非洲国家的进口零关税政策生效，同时因台湾承认问题将斯威士兰排除在外；中美围绕技术和古巴制裁的摩擦仍在延续，中日之间关于军事言论的交锋也没有降温。这说明北京正在同时处理经贸拉拢、台湾议题和大国竞争三条线。
items.rawSummary: China's zero-tariff policy for 53 African nations has taken effect, while Beijing escalates its defiance of U.S. sanctions on Iranian oil and intensifies preparations for a Trump-Xi summit, even as regional tensions with Japan persist.
items.analysis: China's zero-tariff policy for 53 African nations — excluding Eswatini due to its recognition of Taiwan — took effect, reinforcing the One-China principle. The Commerce Ministry's directive to Chinese firms not to comply with U.S. sanctions on oil refiners, alongside the earlier declaration that it does not recognize sanctions on Iranian oil purchases, deepens resistance to what Beijing terms illegal extraterritorial overreach. A forceful Foreign Ministry rebuke of Japan over perceived dangerous military moves has kept regional security tensions prominent. Preparations for the mid-May Trump-Xi summit have accelerated, with two additional U.S. C-17 transport aircraft landing recently, bringing the total number of such aircraft on the ground to four. One of those U.S. planes was spotted alongside an Iranian Mahan Air cargo plane during the preparations, a juxtaposition occurring as China actively challenges U.S. pressure over Iranian oil.

keyPoints.point: China blocks Meta's $2 billion acquisition of AI firm Manus.

China's Foreign Ministry accuses Japan of making dangerous, provocative moves, likening its actions to 'war mobilization and war cries,' and questions whether Japan seeks to repeat history as a source of disaster in East Asia.
China announces tariff-free access for all African countries with diplomatic ties to Beijing, excluding Eswatini because it recognizes Taiwan.
China's Foreign Ministry urges the U.S. to walk back its sanctions regime against Cuba, accusing the U.S. of 'vilifying China-Cuba cooperation.'
China's zero-tariff policy on imports from 53 African countries takes effect; Eswatini is excluded because it recognizes Taiwan.
China states it does not recognize U.S. sanctions on Iranian oil purchases and will not comply with them.
A U.S. military C-17 aircraft lands in Beijing as preparations begin for a meeting between President Trump and President Xi on May 14-15.
China's Ministry of Commerce tells Chinese companies not to comply with U.S. sanctions on certain oil refiners, calling the sanctions illegal extraterritorial overreach.
A U.S. Air Force C-17 and an Iranian Mahan cargo aircraft are spotted alongside each other at Beijing airport.
Two additional U.S. C-17 transport aircraft carrying advance logistics for Trump's China visit land at Beijing Capital Airport, bringing the total number of U.S. military C-17s on the ground to four.

items.title: 巴基斯坦斡旋：伊朗通道与美伊谈判给周边带来变量
items.description: 巴基斯坦不仅是南亚安全变量，也正成为中东外交通道的一部分。WIRE 信息显示，美伊间接谈判继续在伊斯兰堡推进，巴基斯坦还开放了通往伊朗的陆路通道。对中国周边来说，巴基斯坦的角色正在从传统安全延伸到能源通道和地区斡旋。
items.rawSummary: Military and cross-border developments around Pakistan continue, including a missile test, new attack submarines, unconfirmed claims of opened land routes with Iran, ongoing fuel smuggling, and the safe relocation of crew from an Iranian-linked vessel reportedly seized by the U.S.
items.analysis: A training launch of the Fateh-II precision-guided rocket with 400 km range highlights advances in conventional strike options. Pakistan has also reportedly received eight Hangor-class attack submarines, deepening defence cooperation with China. On May 1, a reporter raised the claim that land routes to Iran have been opened; former US President Trump said he was aware and expressed respect for Pakistan’s leadership, though the operational status of any official corridors remains unverified. Fuel smuggling from Iran into Pakistan is reported to continue through informal cross-border routes, even as Iran’s oil sector comes under strain from a U.S.-led blockade that is disrupting exports and forcing crude into storage. The blockade context was further underscored when crew members of an Iranian-linked ship reportedly seized by the U.S. were safely transferred to Pakistan. The coexistence of unconfirmed formal openings and ongoing illicit flows indicates a complex and economically active border region where both overt and covert cross‑border activity may be taking place.

keyPoints.point: Pakistan reportedly conducts a successful training launch of its Fateh-II precision-guided rocket with a 400 km range.
Pakistan reportedly receives 8 Hangor-class attack submarines as part of increased militarization and defence ties with China.
A reporter raises the claim that Pakistan has opened land routes with Iran; former US President Trump acknowledges awareness and voices respect for Pakistan's leadership.
Fuel smuggling from Iran into Pakistan through informal cross-border routes is reported to continue as U.S.-led sanctions pressure Iran's oil sector and disrupt exports.
All crew of an Iranian-linked ship reportedly seized by the U.S. were safely relocated to Pakistan following a maritime operation.

items.title: 韩国：美军考虑把韩国打造为区域支援枢纽
items.description: 韩国方向的重点在美军区域部署。WIRE 信息显示，驻韩美军司令提出把韩国作为区域支援枢纽。这个表述意味着韩国的角色可能从半岛防务进一步外溢到更广泛的印太行动支撑，对中国周边安全结构有长期影响。
items.rawSummary: North Korean women's football team to visit Suwon for Asian Women's Champions League semi-final
items.analysis: North Korea's Naegohyang Women's FC will face South Korea's Suwon FC Women in Suwon on May 20 in the Asian Women's Champions League semi-final. This marks the first visit by North Korean athletes to South Korea since 2018. A 39-member delegation comprising 27 players and 12 staff members is scheduled to arrive on May 17. The event represents a rare inter-Korean sports exchange amid ongoing diplomatic isolation between the two countries.

keyPoints.point: Plans were announced for a North Korean women's football delegation to travel to Suwon, South Korea, for an upcoming Asian Women's Champions League semi-final match — the first such visit since 2018.

items.title: 印度：航空业潜在停摆风险暴露经济压力
items.description: 印度方向出现航空业风险信号。WIRE 信息显示，有关印度航空业可能停摆的警告受到关注。航空业牵动出行、供应链和服务业信心，如果风险继续发酵，可能成为印度经济运行中的一个压力点。
items.rawSummary: Pakistan holds military parade at Indian border on operation anniversary
items.analysis: Pakistan marked the first anniversary of Operation Bunyan Al Marsoos with a military parade near the Indian border. The display was held at the border area, underscoring the military nature of the commemoration. The operation's details were not immediately reported.

keyPoints.point: Pakistan conducts a military parade at the Indian border to mark the anniversary of Operation Bunyan Al Marsoos.

items.title: 霍尔木兹海峡：封锁僵局继续推高能源与航运压力
items.description: 美国海上封锁仍在持续，伊朗方面拒绝把核谈判与重新开放通道直接绑定。WIRE 信息显示，英国海军确认战争爆发以来相关船舶通行量已大幅下降，布伦特原油价格仍处在高位。能源、航运和外交谈判正在相互牵动，这是今天最值得关注的全球风险点。
items.rawSummary: Tensions near the Strait of Hormuz have escalated sharply following an Iranian drone attack on a UAE-owned tanker, with both nations issuing warnings, the U.S. changing rules of engagement and escorting merchant ships, and Iran claiming to fire warning shots at U.S. vessels.
items.analysis: The escalation began when a UAE-owned ADNOC tanker was struck by two Iranian drones, drawing condemnation from the UAE as 'economic blackmail' and 'pirate operations.' In response, the U.S. updated rules of engagement to allow strikes on immediate threats and, according to Axios, ordered strikes on threatening IRGC vessels and positions. CENTCOM announced that two U.S.-flagged merchant ships, trapped since late February by Operation Epic Fury, successfully transited the strait under Project Freedom escort. Iran's IRGC Navy warned that passing ships require Iranian permission, and its regular Navy, through state media Tasnim, claimed to have fired warning shots at U.S. vessels. Meanwhile, five USAF refueling tankers operated over the Persian Gulf with fighter jets likely patrolling the strait, signaling a heightened U.S. air presence as tensions remain at a peak.
items.locationName: 78 nautical miles north of Fujairah, UAE

keyPoints.point: Iranian forces attack at least two MSC-chartered container ships, with both vessels now stopped in Iranian territorial waters; one bridge heavily damaged.
IRGC Navy announces seizure of two vessels, MSC Francesca and Epaminondas, for alleged navigation violations, and directs them to the Iranian coast.
Satellite imagery shows dozens of IRGC speedboats heading in large groups away from the middle of the Strait of Hormuz, suggesting active mining operations are underway.
U.S. officials assess that clearing the strait of mines could take up to six months, with operations unlikely until a long-term ceasefire is in place.

The White House Press Secretary states the U.S. does not view the Iranian seizure of the two vessels as a ceasefire violation, downplaying the incidents as piracy and claiming Iran's conventional navy has been destroyed.
IRGC Navy releases footage of its forces boarding and seizing two container ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

Analysis indicates IRGC Commander Vahidi is prepared to resume the war if needed to assert Iranian control over the strait, as Iranian decision-making remains fragmented and unable to formulate a coherent negotiating position.
Iran announces it has received its first official revenue from transit tolls imposed on vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz, reportedly up to $2 million per passage.

Hardline IRGC generals, led by Vahidi, have overwhelmed political figures in internal debates, causing the collapse of recent negotiations, while Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei remains in hiding and has delegated authority to hardliners.
President Trump orders the U.S. Navy to shoot and destroy any Iranian boats laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz and triples mine-clearing operations.

Trump asserts the U.S. has total control over the Strait of Hormuz and that no ship can enter or leave without U.S. approval, citing infighting between Iranian hardliners and moderates, and suggests he does not need a deal with Iran.

The world's top 10 tanker and containership owners have completely stopped their ships from attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz, prioritizing getting vessels out of the region amid continued Iranian seizures.
CENTCOM reports that 33 vessels have been directed back to Iranian ports or turned back since the start of the U.S. blockade of vessels traveling to and from Iranian ports.

The U.S. has used over 1,000 Tomahawk missiles and thousands of air-defense interceptors in the Iran war, raising concerns that restocking could take up to six years, potentially affecting readiness for other contingencies such as a Taiwan scenario.

Heads of Iran's three branches of government and other senior officials publicly reject the existence of 'hardline' and 'moderate' factions, circulating unifying revolutionary slogans to defend against potential accusations of moderation from hardliners like Vahidi.

The US military is preparing plans to strike Iran's defenses around the Strait of Hormuz if the current ceasefire fails, with targets potentially including small attack boats, mine-laying vessels, missiles, and drones, as well as energy infrastructure or Iranian military leaders.

Two more tankers cross the Strait of Hormuz: China-owned oil tanker Well Sail and Singapore-owned, US-sanctioned LPG tanker Avon, indicating limited but continued traffic despite the blockade and mining.

Hegseth announces that a second U.S. aircraft carrier will join the blockade in several days, and authorizes shoot-to-destroy rules of engagement against Iranian forces laying mines or threatening U.S. ships.
Chairman of the Joint Chiefs General Caine reports the U.S. has now directed 34 vessels to turn back that are traveling to and from Iranian ports.
U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth says Europe needs the Strait of Hormuz much more than the U.S. does, signaling potential shifts in allied burden-sharing.
Hegseth criticizes Asian and European allies for not joining the Iran War or assisting in clearing the strait, stating 'the time for free-riding is over.'
German Chancellor Merz conditions any sanctions relief on free navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, a definitive end to Iran's nuclear program, and an end to Iranian threats against Israel.
CENTCOM announces the USS George H.W. Bush has entered the region, with over 200 aircraft and twelve ships now operating in the area.
Two oil tankers, the Indian-registered and OFAC-sanctioned 'OCEANJET' and the unknown-ownership 'LUMINA OCEAN', cross the Strait of Hormuz with IRGC authorization.
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan says Türkiye may join demining efforts in the Strait of Hormuz after a potential Iran–U.S. deal, calling it a 'humanitarian duty' in principle.

Iran's Central Headquarters of Hazrat Khatam al-Anbiya warns the U.S. that continued siege and maritime operations will face a reaction from Iran's armed forces, claiming greater readiness and offensive capability than before and threatening to inflict heavier damages.
Iranian state television visits the seized container ship Epaminondas in the Strait of Hormuz, with the MSC Francesca confirmed still nearby and AIS tracking off since April 22.

Iranian-flagged and U.S.-sanctioned bulk carrier PARISA departs the Strait of Hormuz for China, with its movements intentionally kept visible in what appears to be a display of defiance against the blockade.
Russian oligarch's super yacht 'The Nord' crosses the Strait of Hormuz with IRGC permission, after departing Dubai.
U.S. naval forces turn back $1.05 billion of Iranian crude and the U.S. Coast Guard seizes $380 million at sea, intensifying economic pressure on Iran.
Iran reportedly offers a new proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and lift the U.S. blockade first, with nuclear talks to be delayed.
U.S. President Trump and UK Prime Minister Starmer hold a call discussing the 'urgent need' to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, signaling high-level allied coordination on the crisis.
A US Army AH-64E Apache attack helicopter returns from a mission over the Strait of Hormuz, indicating expanded aerial surveillance and strike capability alongside naval forces.

U.S. aircraft carriers operating in the region are reported to depend on the Saudi port of Yanbu, the UAE port of Fujairah, and the Omani port of Duqm for supplies, potentially creating logistical vulnerabilities.

The United States continues moving military equipment to the Middle East amid the ceasefire, and the U.S., Israel, and Iran are reportedly preparing for a possible new round of war if no deal is reached.
President Trump expresses skepticism regarding Iran's offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and delay nuclear talks, according to a Wall Street Journal report.
Marco Rubio states that Iran cannot be the sole beneficiaries of an illegal, unlawful, and unjustified system of tolling and control in the straits.

Prediction market Polymarket shows the likelihood of normal traffic resumption in the Strait of Hormuz before the end of next month has dropped to 40%, with warnings of potential fuel shortages if the strait remains closed for five more weeks.

President Trump told advisers he is not satisfied with Iran’s latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which calls for lifting the U.S. blockade and postponing nuclear talks, according to The New York Times.
Two Japan-owned oil tankers, STARWAY and IDEMITSU MARU, cross the Strait of Hormuz with IRGC permission.
The first shipment of liquefied natural gas crosses the Strait of Hormuz since the war began, according to Bloomberg.

Russian oligarch Alexei Mordashov's superyacht 'Nord' crossed the Strait of Hormuz heading to Oman with IRGC permission, confirming the 142-meter sanctioned vessel transited despite the blockade and mine threat.

According to MarineTraffic.com data, several vessels have passed through the Strait of Hormuz in the last 12 hours, most using the Iranian traffic separation scheme that forces traffic well north of the internationally recognized traffic separation scheme.
President Trump posts on Truth Social that Iran has informed the U.S. it is in a 'State of Collapse' and wants the Strait of Hormuz opened as soon as possible.

ISW-CTP analysis details that Iran’s latest proposal is unchanged from previous offers: a three-stage plan demanding a permanent end to the war and U.S. blockade lift, then negotiations over Iranian tolling and management of the Strait of Hormuz, with no nuclear concessions.
U.S. gas prices rise to about $4.18 per gallon, the highest since 2022, and oil prices have surged over 40% since February amid tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, according to The New York Times.

Gulf urea production falls to a new low of about 160,000 tons per week, down roughly 60% since the Iran War began, with 44 fertilizer vessels stuck inside the Gulf and only 11 having transited the Strait of Hormuz, prompting warnings of accelerating global food inflation, according to The Kobeissi Letter.

President Trump has told aides to prepare for an extended U.S. blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, according to the Wall Street Journal citing U.S. officials, viewing pulling out or resuming combat operations against Iran as riskier than continuing to interdict vessels traveling to and from Iranian ports.
The U.S. blockade has resulted in the lowest number of transits through the Strait of Hormuz since the Iran War began, which today reaches its two-month mark, according to the Wall Street Journal.
Polymarket now predicts only a 36% chance that normal maritime traffic will resume in the Strait of Hormuz by the end of May, down from 40% on April 27, reflecting continued deadlock in negotiations.
Japan's Prime Minister confirms that a Japanese-related vessel safely passed through the Strait of Hormuz on April 29.

A China-owned oil tanker VAST PLUS, whose owner is under U.S. sanctions for buying Iranian oil, crosses the Strait of Hormuz; China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated the day before it will defend Chinese companies' lawful rights.

German Chancellor Merz expresses doubts about the Iran war from the start, states Germany and Europe are suffering severely from the Strait of Hormuz closure, and says he is pushing for the conflict to be resolved.

US oil prices surge above $103 per barrel for the first time since April 13, with the Kobeissi Letter noting the rise comes amid reports of Trump preparing an extended blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian state media warns of 'unprecedented military action' if U.S. seizures of Iranian-linked vessels continue, as reported by the Kobeissi Letter, while Brent crude nears $114 per barrel.
White House officials say President Trump has discussed with US oil companies a plan to potentially continue the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz for months.
US oil prices extend gains to $105 per barrel as President Trump prepares to extend the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz for months.
President Trump rejects the Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, stating the U.S. blockade will continue until Iran agrees to a nuclear deal, according to Axios.
CENTCOM has prepared plans for a short, powerful wave of strikes against Iran to pressure Tehran into negotiations, Axios reports, as the blockade has not yet forced Iran to change its position.

Brent crude oil prices surge to $119.50 per barrel, their highest level of the Iran War and the highest since 2022, with the International Energy Agency calling it the 'biggest energy security threat in history.'
Secretary of State Marco Rubio and UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper met to discuss restoring freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, according to a State Department release.

CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper announces the U.S. has now directed 42 vessels to turn back from Iranian ports since the blockade began, with 200 aircraft and 25 ships involved in the operation.
The Wall Street Journal reports that the Trump administration is asking other countries to join a new international coalition to help open the Strait of Hormuz.
The U.S. Army is reportedly considering taking control of part of the Strait of Hormuz to restore passage.
Reuters reported that the U.S. has continued heavy pressure on Europe to form a coalition to restore international freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei states that the Persian Gulf will be 'without America' and Iran will exercise control over the Strait of Hormuz through a new legal framework, warning that outsiders with 'greedy intentions' have no place there except 'at the bottom of its waters.'
German Chancellor Merz states Germany is ready to engage militarily, if necessary conditions are met, to quickly end Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian denounces the U.S. naval blockade as an extension of military operations and calls the continued oppressive approach intolerable.

U.S. Senator Lindsey Graham proposes a 'blockade plus' strategy: continue the blockade but open a lane in the Strait of Hormuz to reduce Iranian leverage, and let Admiral Cooper finish his target list if Iran continues provocations.

MarineTraffic.com playback over the last 24 hours shows that some transits are occurring, mostly using the Iranian traffic separation scheme, and daily traffic volume remains less than 10% of the pre-war average of 130 vessels per day.
The British Navy reports that ship passage through the Strait of Hormuz has dropped 90% since the start of the war.
Exxon CEO Darren Woods says it will take 1-2 months for normal maritime flows to resume after the Strait of Hormuz reopens.
Iran claimed that the Strait of Hormuz is not an international waterway but an Iranian right.
The U.S. warns shippers that paying tolls for passage through the Strait of Hormuz risks sanctions.
President Trump accused adversaries of attempting to disrupt global trade by threatening closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
President Trump has reportedly rejected a new Iranian peace proposal that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz but leave nuclear talks for later.
Satellite imagery captures several dozen Iranian gunboats operating around the middle of the Strait of Hormuz, indicating mine-laying or patrol activity just north of Oman.
Reuters reported, citing an Iranian official, that President Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and delay nuclear talks.
Approximately 40 Iranian speedboats were spotted in the Strait of Hormuz possibly laying mines.
Axios reports that Iran's proposal set a one-month deadline for negotiations on a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, end the U.S. naval blockade, and permanently end the war in Iran and Lebanon.
Security assessments have concluded that Iran is heavily mining the Strait of Hormuz during the ceasefire.
CENTCOM reports it has redirected at least 48 Iranian-linked ships into and out of the Strait of Hormuz so far.
The IRGC threatens that the Strait of Hormuz will become a 'graveyard' for U.S. 'pirates.'

Reuters reports that Iran's 14-point proposal includes lifting blockades and sanctions, removing U.S. forces, releasing frozen assets, compensating Iran, and ending the war in Lebanon, clashing with Washington's demand that Iran first give up its more than 400 kg of highly enriched uranium.
Iran rejects nuclear talks in the first phase of a peace agreement, demanding sanctions relief and compensation before lifting the Strait of Hormuz blockade.

N12 reports on an emerging U.S.-Iran deal framework that includes a regional ceasefire, gradual reopening of the Strait, Iranian mine-clearing with U.S. assistance, a 15-year uranium enrichment freeze, and eventual sanctions removal.
CENTCOM reports that 49 commercial vessels have been redirected to comply with the blockade, with U.S. forces committed to total enforcement.
Tracking data shows that out of 25 Iranian oil tankers in April, 16 made it past the U.S. blockade, while 7 turned back, 2 were seized, and 1 completed delivery.
A cargo ship was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz west of Sirik, Iran; the crew was reported safe.
Senior UAE official Reem Al Hashimy states that no one should control the Strait of Hormuz, emphasizing that geography necessitates coexistence and mutual accommodation.
Al Jazeera reports that an Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman's advisor said Iran will coordinate with neighboring nations and coastal states regarding the Strait of Hormuz situation.
A senior Iranian lawmaker announced that a new law will establish conditions for transit through the Strait of Hormuz.
A senior Iranian lawmaker stated that Israeli vessels will be completely barred from passing through the Strait of Hormuz under any circumstances.
President Trump announced Project Freedom, an initiative to guide neutral countries' ships out of the Strait of Hormuz starting Monday, warning that interference would be met with force.

U.S. Senator Lindsey Graham endorsed Project Freedom, calling Iran's latest negotiation offer 'absurd' and asserting that it is time to 'regain freedom of navigation' and forcefully respond to Iran 'terrorizing the world.'
US oil prices fell below $100 per barrel after President Trump announced Project Freedom to guide ships through the Strait of Hormuz.

Ebrahim Azizi, head of Iran's parliament national security committee, warned that any American interference in the new maritime regime of the Strait of Hormuz will be considered a violation of the ceasefire, and said the strait will not be managed by Trump's 'delusional posts' and no one would believe 'Blame Game scenarios.'

The Wall Street Journal reports that the U.S. mission to guide ships out of the Strait of Hormuz will not involve Navy escorts; instead, ships will be given instructions on safe passage routes and coordination with shipping and insurance companies.
U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) announced it will support Project Freedom.
U.S. Central Command stated that Project Freedom will involve over 100 land- and sea-based aircraft, guided missile destroyers, unmanned platforms, and 15,000 U.S. servicemembers.
U.S. naval vessels will reportedly be positioned to intervene if Iranian forces attempt to challenge transiting ships.
UKMTO reported that another tanker was hit by multiple projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz area.
UKMTO reported that a tanker was hit by unknown projectiles 78 nautical miles north of Fujairah, UAE; all crew are safe and authorities are investigating.
President Trump stated that the U.S. will start escorting ships stuck in the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz from Monday and warned that any interference will be responded to forcefully.
Iran's armed forces command warned that the U.S. Navy should not approach or enter the Strait of Hormuz.
UKMTO reported that a bulk carrier was attacked by multiple small craft 11NM west of Sirik, Iran; crew safe and no damage reported.

Iran’s armed forces command escalated its warning, stating it would attack any U.S. military vessels that approach the Strait of Hormuz and warning commercial ships not to cross without Iranian approval.
An Iranian military commander claimed that Iran fully controls the Strait of Hormuz and will respond harshly to any foreign military approach, Fars reported.

U.S. Central Command announced that Project Freedom will launch on May 4 and includes a new diplomatic initiative called the Maritime Freedom Construct to coordinate with partners, alongside the previously announced military assets.
Iranian Major General Abdollahi warned that any foreign military force approaching the Strait of Hormuz will be targeted and that commercial ships must coordinate transit with Iranian forces.

UKMTO reported that a new U.S. security corridor is now in place in the Strait of Hormuz, directing vessels to sail south of old traffic lanes, closer to Oman's coast, following President Trump's launch of Project Freedom.
Iranian officials stated that U.S. military escorts for vessels through the Strait of Hormuz are unacceptable.
The IRGC released new maps outlining the zones it claims to control in the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran stated it is ready to respond to 'U.S. threats' in the Strait of Hormuz and said shipping companies must coordinate with Iranian authorities for their security.

The IRGC warned that any foreign military, especially U.S., attempting to approach or enter the Strait of Hormuz will be attacked, and that civilian and commercial ships can pass safely only if they comply with Iranian naval rules and coordinate movement.

Iranian state-backed outlets reported that the Iranian Armed Forces claimed to have prevented a U.S. destroyer from entering the Strait of Hormuz; the IRGC stated that a warning from the Iranian Navy stopped an 'American Zionist destroyer.'
An IRGC spokesperson said that vessels failing to coordinate transit with Iran will be 'stopped with force.'
Axios reported a U.S. official saying that U.S. forces will destroy any Iranian boats and missiles attempting to attack shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
Local sources and Iranian media made unverified claims that two missiles hit a U.S. navy vessel in the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran's Fars news agency reported that two missiles were fired at a U.S. Navy vessel near the Strait of Hormuz, causing damage and forcing it to retreat.
Axios reported that President Trump has grown frustrated with the 'no deal, no war' stalemate and is pushing for more decisive action in the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy published a map showing a newly defined zone in the Strait of Hormuz extending from near Kuh Mobarak in Iran to south of Fujairah in the UAE.
A senior U.S. official denied that a U.S. ship was hit by Iranian missiles, according to Axios.
The Iranian Navy declared a 'new control zone' in the Strait of Hormuz.
The Spokesman of Iran's National Security Council stated that the Strait of Hormuz is under Iranian control and can only be opened by accepting Iran's sovereignty or returning to the battlefield.
CNN reported that only one sanctioned tanker transited the Strait of Hormuz on May 4, with no other tankers or cargo ships moving through.

U.S. Central Command denied Iranian media claims of a U.S. warship being hit, stating no U.S. Navy ships have been struck and that U.S. forces are supporting Project Freedom and enforcing a naval blockade on Iranian ports.
A vessel belonging to UAE's Adnoc was reportedly hit by two Iranian drones in the Strait of Hormuz.
Reuters cited a senior Iranian official stating that warning shots were fired at a U.S. Navy vessel in the Strait of Hormuz.
The UAE Foreign Ministry condemned the Iranian drone attack on an ADNOC oil tanker, blaming the IRGC and calling it 'economic blackmail that amounts to piracy,' with no injuries reported.
A U.S. official stated that rules of engagement have been updated to allow American forces to strike immediate threats in the Strait of Hormuz, including IRGC boats and Iranian missile sites.
The IRGC Navy warned ships in the Strait of Hormuz that passing through requires Iranian permission and that vessels without permission would be struck and destroyed.

Anwar Gargash, diplomatic advisor to the UAE President, condemned the Iranian drone attack on an ADNOC tanker, describing it as 'pirate operations' and reaffirming the UAE's rejection of aggression and commitment to protecting freedom of navigation.
The U.S. military stated that two U.S.-flagged merchant vessels successfully transited the Strait of Hormuz.

CENTCOM announced that two U.S.-flagged merchant vessels trapped in the Persian Gulf since February 28 due to Operation Epic Fury have transited the Strait of Hormuz outbound under Project Freedom, with U.S. guided-missile destroyers now operating in the Arabian Gulf.
Axios reported that the U.S. ordered its military to strike any IRGC naval vessels and missile positions that pose an immediate threat to ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran's Navy, via state outlet Tasnim, claimed it fired warning shots at U.S. Navy vessels near the Strait of Hormuz.
Fighter jets were likely patrolling the Strait of Hormuz and five USAF refueling tankers operated over the Persian Gulf amid reports of new U.S. rules of engagement authorizing strikes on threats.

items.title: 伊朗战局：美方宣称敌对行动终止，但军事压力并未消失
items.description: 尽管美国以战争权力程序为由声称敌对状态已经结束，WIRE 信息显示，海上封锁仍在继续冲击伊朗经济，美方也仍在讨论潜在的进一步军事选项。与此同时，伊朗内部路线分歧和强硬表态交织，使局势离真正降温仍有距离。
items.rawSummary: Iran faces intensifying economic strain from the U.S. naval blockade and regional military pressure as diplomatic talks remain deadlocked, with both sides weighing further military action, while domestic repression and surging medicine prices compound internal hardship.
items.analysis: Now in its third month, the U.S. naval blockade is straining Iran's economy, with oil storage near capacity, the rial at record lows, and production cuts underway. Diplomatic channels remain deadlocked: President Trump has indicated a 'possibility' of resuming strikes, Iran has submitted both a 14-point plan reported by Axios and a 3-stage proposal reported by Al Jazeera, and the IRGC frames Trump's choices as an 'impossible' military operation or a bad deal. Israeli military assessments see a rising likelihood of renewed fighting, with Yedioth Ahronoth reporting that Washington is weighing a rapid, high-impact strike and considering ground operations, as Israeli Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir intensifies contacts with CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper and Israeli officials told News 14 that a return to fighting is a matter of 'when, not if.' Strikes have disrupted IRGC-linked cryptocurrency mining, temporarily easing blackouts, while Iranian state media claimed UAE fighter jets took part in airstrikes, an allegation that would mark a regional escalation if confirmed. Domestically, the government executed three men for January protest involvement, and state TV reported that essential drug prices have tripled, compounding public hardship as external pressures mount.

keyPoints.point: Reports emerge of deep divisions within Iranian leadership between hardline IRGC generals who view negotiations as futile under the U.S. blockade and political figures who argue for a negotiated settlement to relieve economic pressure, with the hardliners currently prevailing.
Mojtaba Khamenei remains in hiding surrounded by military staff, having delegated significant autonomy to extreme IRGC generals who are pushing hardline negotiating positions.

The New York Times reports, citing Iranian officials, that Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is gravely wounded from an earlier strike, having undergone multiple leg surgeries, suffered facial burns, and is slowly regaining function, communicating only through sealed handwritten messages relayed by couriers.

The New York Times reports that Khamenei's delegation of decision-making powers to his generals, due to his incapacitation, has allowed them to gain disproportionate influence in Iran's decision-making process.
President Trump issues a public warning to Iran, stating 'the clock is ticking' and asserting he has all the time in the world while Iran does not.

President Trump states the U.S. has hit about 75 percent of its targets and that a blockade is 100 percent effective, but also that Iran wants a deal and the U.S. has been speaking to them, though Tehran does not know who is leading the country.
Iran's internet blackout reaches 56 consecutive days, with international connectivity severed for more than 1,320 hours, according to NetBlocks.

The Wall Street Journal reports that the U.S. has begun signaling it will allow some Iranian enrichment in negotiations, demanding a 20-year suspension but open to enrichment in the second decade, while Iran has countered with a 5-year suspension request.

Trump issues a three-day ultimatum, warning that Iran's oil infrastructure will be destroyed within that timeframe, significantly escalating the coercive pressure and setting a near-term deadline for compliance.

Bloomberg reports that Iran is running out of onshore oil storage capacity with only 12 to 22 days remaining, as the U.S. naval blockade has cut exports by roughly 70% and nearly halted tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz; Iran may be forced to cut production by another 1.5 million barrels per day by mid-May.
The New York Times reports, citing European intelligence, that Russia is preparing to deliver highly advanced drones to Iran.

Intelligence reports indicate Iran has used the ceasefire to redeploy and unbury many of its drone and missile capabilities, spreading them across the country in preparation for a continuation of mass strikes.
The Iranian rial drops to a new record low of 1.8 million IRR per USD, with the U.S.-led naval blockade costing Iran up to $500 million in lost revenue daily and annual inflation exceeding 40%.
The U.S. Central Command has readied a strike plan targeting Iranian infrastructure, with strikes expected as soon as tomorrow.
Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei vowed to sink American ships to the 'bottom of its waters.'
Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf mockingly highlighted the length of Iran's borders to dismiss the U.S. naval blockade as impractical.

Fox News reports that CENTCOM Admiral Brad Cooper has briefed President Trump on 'final blow' strike options against Iran, with assessed targets including remaining military equipment, regime/IRGC leadership, and infrastructure.
A Washington Post-ABC-Ipsos poll found that 61% of Americans call the war with Iran a mistake, with disapproval reaching levels comparable to the Iraq War at its peak.
Surging jet fuel prices amid the Iran conflict have reportedly derailed Spirit Airlines' attempt to emerge from bankruptcy, costing the airline an additional $10–15 million per week in fuel expenses.

Strikes reportedly disrupted IRGC-linked cryptocurrency mining operations, which had been a major driver of Iran's power blackouts; the reduction in mining demand led to a temporary stabilization of the electricity grid and surplus power.
President Trump stated there is a 'possibility' of resuming strikes against Iran.

Iran submitted a 14-point proposal to the United States outlining a two-stage plan: first, negotiate a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, lift the U.S. naval blockade, and end the wars in Iran and Lebanon; second, begin talks on Iran's nuclear program, according to Axios.
The IRGC states that President Trump faces a binary choice between an 'impossible' military operation and accepting what it calls a bad deal with Iran.
Senior Iranian military and security officials have expressed pessimism about the prospects for compromise between Iran and the United States.

Al Jazeera reported that Iran proposed a 3-stage plan to end the war: a permanent ceasefire, gradual reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and lifting of the U.S. blockade, a nuclear deal freezing enrichment and capping it later at civilian level, and regional security talks.
Senior Israeli officials told News 14 that a return to fighting in Iran requires readiness and is a question of 'when, not if.'
U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche stated that the United States is engaged in a military operation in Iran, not a war.
Iranian state media claimed UAE fighter jets took part in airstrikes on Iran.
Iran's regime announced the execution of three men over their involvement in protests that took place in January.
Iranian state TV reported that essential drug prices have tripled, with items once costing 100,000 toman now reaching 300,000 toman.
Yedioth Ahronoth reported that Israel assesses the chances of renewed fighting with Iran are rising, as Washington weighs a rapid, high-impact strike and considers ground operations.

items.title: 伊朗内部：强硬派主导谈判立场，核协议预期降温
items.description: 伊朗政权内部的强硬路线仍占上风，围绕防空能力、核谈判和外交让步的信号相互矛盾。市场此前对核协议的乐观预期正在减弱，说明外部压力并未换来清晰的妥协路径。
items.rawSummary: Iran and the U.S. remain locked in a diplomatic standoff over Iran's three-phase proposal, with the rial hitting rock bottom, war planning taking precedence, and fresh executions underscoring domestic repression.
items.analysis: Iran confirmed it received a U.S. response via Pakistan and is reviewing it, while Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei characterized the reply as containing excessive and unreasonable demands, though details remain under consideration. President Trump dismissed the proposal as unacceptable, warned that combat operations remain possible, and the U.S. naval blockade continues. Economic strain is worsening with the rial at a historic low, and a high-level meeting focused entirely on war scenarios rather than diplomacy signals that the IRGC's influence is paramount. Hardline rhetoric persists alongside repression: three men linked to the January protests have been executed, adding to two earlier executions for alleged Mossad spying. Israel remains on alert for a possible U.S. strike or Iranian preemptive action and is coordinating with CENTCOM.

keyPoints.point: The White House stated the U.S. does not consider Iran's seizure of two ships to be a violation of the ceasefire and clarified that public reports of a firm 3-5 day deadline are not true.
The White House reiterated the U.S. demand for Iran to turn over its enriched uranium.
U.S. officials identified a complete split within the Iranian leadership between moderates pushing for talks and hardliners taking a hardline approach.
Unconfirmed reports of explosions and air defense activity east of Tehran were attributed by Iranian sources to military exercises and air defense tests.

A pro-regime protest in Tehran featured the Spanish flag, signaling international solidarity with Iran's anti-U.S. stance, as Spain refused a U.S. request to use its military bases and closed its airspace to U.S. aircraft.

Reports indicate that Mojtaba Khamenei has undergone three surgeries on one leg and may require a prosthetic, and also suffered severe burns and hand surgery, permanently maiming him and raising questions about leadership succession.

The United States intercepted and boarded a sanctioned oil tanker in the Indian Ocean and redirected three Iranian-flagged tankers near India, Malaysia, and Sri Lanka, expanding the maritime blockade far beyond the Gulf of Oman.
New reports of air defense activity over Parand in Tehran province indicated heightened readiness.
Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf resigned from the negotiating team after reported intervention by the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, underscoring hardliner dominance.
Reports emerged that Iran's air defense was firing at hostile targets in Tehran, though Israeli officials denied any involvement, suggesting the activity may be performative for pro-regime marches.
An explosion was reported in the Sattarkhan district of Tehran, adding to unconfirmed incidents in the capital.
Iran announced it has decided not to enter negotiations with the US and denied making any request for direct talks, per state-aligned Tasnim news agency.
Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman stated no meeting is planned between Iran and the U.S., and any communication will be relayed through Pakistan.

The U.S. Treasury's OFAC announced new sanctions targeting Iran's oil trade and shadow fleet, including sanctions on China-based refinery Hengli Petrochemical (Dalian), 19 tankers, and crypto wallets used by the Central Bank of Iran.
Iran stated it still has significant missile capabilities that have not been used yet, signaling continued escalation capacity.

Analysis indicates that pragmatic officials may continue advocating for flexibility but are unlikely to shape regime decision-making near-term, with IRGC commander Vahidi's victory over Ghalibaf likely impacting future US-Iran negotiations.
Imam Khamenei International Airport in Tehran reopened to limited flights.
Iranian negotiators reportedly passed messages to the US asking President Trump to tone down his threats, believing that hardliners would be more open to negotiations if American pressure eased.
Iran proposed a deal to the U.S. to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, extend a ceasefire, and postpone nuclear negotiations until later, signaling a more concrete diplomatic outreach.

Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that incorrect approaches and excessive demands by the U.S. caused the previous round of talks to fail despite progress, publicly acknowledging negotiations while shifting blame to Washington.

European Commission President von der Leyen said it is too early to lift sanctions on Iran, insisting that fundamental change in Iran must come first, complicating Tehran's efforts to court European allies and gain sanctions relief.

Iran's new offer to mediators reportedly outlines a 3-phase peace plan beginning with ending the war and ensuring it does not resume, and explicitly mentions Iran's intent to retain control over the Strait of Hormuz.
Smuggled footage published by the New York Post shows six protesters being executed while defiantly singing, exposing the regime's violent suppression of internal dissent.

Trump and his national security team are skeptical of Iran's latest proposal, questioning whether it is acting in good faith and willing to end uranium enrichment, but the White House will continue talks and is expected to present counterproposals, per the Wall Street Journal.

ISW analysis indicates Iran is exploiting its Strait of Hormuz leverage to secure an end to the U.S. blockade without making nuclear concessions, a push partly driven by rapidly depleting oil storage capacity forced by the blockade; IRGC commander Vahidi's support for the proposal remains unclear.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi returned to Tehran after meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg.
Trump is unhappy with Iran's latest proposal because it delays nuclear negotiations, and the U.S. insists nuclear issues must be addressed immediately, leaving both sides far apart, per Reuters.

Iran's deputy Defence Minister Brigadier General Reza Talaei-Nik stated, via state-aligned Tasnim, that the US is no longer in a position to dictate policies and that Iran is ready to share its defensive military capabilities with Shanghai Cooperation Organization members.
Several advisors privately told Trump that only resuming military action would break the deadlock with Iran.
An Israeli official stated after a high-level security briefing that the Iranian regime is about to pay a very heavy price, calling for patience and alertness.

A photo circulated showing an Iranian woman mocking the Islamic regime's 'feminist propaganda' by wearing a hijab and holding a TV frame reading IRGC TV propaganda, referencing recent women-only rallies in Tehran featuring pink military vehicles and weapons in an attempt to appeal to Western audiences.

U.S. intelligence agencies are assessing how Iran might respond if Trump declares victory and scales back the war, with early assessments suggesting Iran could see a U.S. withdrawal as a win, per Reuters.
Iran has used the ceasefire to recover and redeploy launchers, drones, and munitions previously buried by U.S. and Israeli strikes, per Reuters.

The U.S. Treasury Department announced additional sanctions targeting Iranian banking networks that fund the regime and the IRGC, including private companies known as 'Rahbars' that assist blacklisted banks in using shadow banking to support the Armed Forces General Staff, National Iranian Oil Company, and IRGC.
President Trump posted on Truth Social stating "NO MORE MR. NICE GUY!" and that Iran "better get smart soon," urging Iran to sign a non-nuclear deal.
Trump's advisors told him a nuclear deal with Iran is unlikely, and Trump instructed them to prepare for an indefinite blockade until Iran capitulates, per the Wall Street Journal.

Sources inside Iranian leadership told Reuters that the IRGC military wing has completely taken over military and political decision-making, with the newly appointed leader only able to ratify decisions rather than issue directives.

The new leadership structure is described as a collective wartime leadership centered on the IRGC and Supreme National Security Council, with Mojtaba Khamenei as nominal supreme leader endorsing decisions but not making them, and hardline military figures now driving policy, per Reuters.

Former Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, previously ousted from the negotiating team by the IRGC, stated the enemy has entered a new phase aiming to activate maritime blockade, media warfare, economic pressure, and internal division to weaken or collapse the country from within.
Iranian Navy Chief stated that a weapon they deeply fear will soon be revealed at their doorstep.
Senior Iranian official Mohsen Rezaee stated Iran will not tolerate the naval blockade and warned that if it continues, Iran will respond.
Unconfirmed reports of explosions in Iran, including Tehran, with the cause unclear at this stage.
Significant air-defense activity and explosions were reported over Tehran; both U.S. and Israeli officials denied renewed strikes against Iran.
Iran's Navy Commander warned that Iran will soon confront its enemies with a 'very dreadful weapon.'

Iran's upcoming proposal to the U.S. is expected to refuse meaningful concessions on the Strait of Hormuz and nuclear program, as the regime coalesces behind IRGC commander Ahmad Vahidi's hardline approach.
Oman rejected an Iranian proposal to involve it in a toll-collection scheme aimed at legitimizing Iran's control over the Strait of Hormuz.
The U.S. Army is reportedly considering contingency plans to seize Iran's enriched uranium stockpile.
A Pentagon official said the US war against Iran has cost $25 billion so far.
Professor Robert Pape assessed that Iran is likely laying the groundwork for nuclear weapons, working with Pakistan and Russia, and positioning itself as a major center of global power.
German Chancellor Merz demanded that Iran stop playing for time, end its military nuclear program, and cease strikes against Israel and regional partners.
Reportedly, Iran's leadership seeks the removal of Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi over the handling of nuclear negotiations.
Polymarket estimated a 33 percent chance of a permanent US-Iran peace deal by June 30, reflecting market skepticism amid the ceasefire and blockade.
US officials told CBS News that the true cost of the Iran war is closer to $50 billion, exceeding an earlier Pentagon estimate of $25 billion.
Air defense activity was reported over southern Tehran.
The UAE called on its citizens to immediately depart Iran, Iraq, and Lebanon.
President Trump stated that the blockade on Iran has been '100% effective'.
Iranian air defense was reportedly intercepting reconnaissance drones and quadcopters in the skies over Tehran.
President Trump threatened to seize Iran's nuclear material by force and claimed that Iranian leaders are dead and Tehran has no functioning air defense.
Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei declared that Iran will retain control over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and maintain its nuclear and missile capabilities.

Two informed sources reported that Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has been acting in full coordination with IRGC commander Ahmad Vahidi and following his instructions, while Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf and President Pezeshkian are reportedly dissatisfied with this alignment.

Polymarket odds of a nuclear deal with Iran by the end of 2026 fell sharply to 53 percent, down over 15 percentage points in a day, amid rising oil prices and growing likelihood of renewed US-Iran hostilities.
President Trump was briefed by U.S. Central Command Commander Admiral Brad Cooper on military options with Iran.
EuroPost noted that Trump's assertions about Iran's air defenses and leadership have not been independently verified.
Iran called on Gulf states to pay damages, accusing them of aiding the U.S. and Israel in the war.
Iran sent a new peace proposal to the U.S. on Thursday, but sources said it still does not address enrichment issues or proxy support, per Reuters.
The Wall Street Journal reported that Iran is attempting to redirect 40 percent of its oil exports by rail to China and import food through the Caucasus mountains to circumvent the naval blockade.

Moderate factions reportedly believe seeking a deal now with a Trump administration eager to exit the war could yield favorable terms, while hardline military factions argue for renewed hostilities to further raise oil prices and pressure Washington.
U.S. Envoy Witkoff reportedly sent amendments to restore nuclear terms, including a requirement that Iran not move enriched uranium or restart bombed sites during talks.
A fire was reported in western Tehran.
The U.S. Treasury issued new Iran-related sanctions.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent stated that the U.S. has complete control of the Strait of Hormuz, there is a hard currency shortage, food and gasoline rationing, the international community has turned against Iran, and the blockade will continue until pre-February 27 freedom of navigation is restored.
President Trump stated he is not satisfied with Iran's latest peace proposal and doubted a deal will be reached, describing Iran's leadership as very disjointed with multiple groups.
Trump stated that talks with Iran are being conducted by phone.
Trump expressed displeasure with Italy and Spain, claiming they feel it is acceptable for Iran to have a nuclear weapon.
Trump claimed that even hardliners in Iran want to make a deal because they have nothing.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Iran has eased its stance to restart peace talks, dropping its demand that the U.S. lift the blockade before negotiations and proposing simultaneous discussion of the Strait of Hormuz and sanctions relief, though the two sides remain far apart on its nuclear program.
Iran announced the execution of two people convicted of spying for Israel's Mossad.

Channel 12 reported that Israel is preparing for the possibility of an imminent U.S. strike on Iran and a potential preemptive Iranian attack, with the Israeli Chief of Staff having contacted CENTCOM Commander Cooper to coordinate.

Iran submitted a 14-point counterproposal to the U.S. through Pakistani mediation, per Tasnim, demanding a complete end to the war within 30 days, including withdrawal of U.S. forces, lifting the naval blockade, sanctions relief, compensation, and new Strait of Hormuz rules, while the U.S. had proposed a 2-month ceasefire.
President Trump stated that resuming combat operations against Iran remains a possibility.

President Trump described the naval blockade as 'very friendly' and unchallenged, and criticized Congress for actions he said hurt his negotiating ability, while responding to a reporter's question about his letter to Congress stating that hostilities with Iran have been terminated.
President Trump stated he will review Iran's plan but cannot imagine it would be acceptable.

Axios reported that Iran proposed a phased roadmap to the U.S., with an initial 30-day de-escalation phase to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, lift the naval blockade, and halt fighting, followed by a second phase of nuclear negotiations.
The Iranian rial hit a record low against the US dollar, with one USD worth 1,910,000 rials.
Iran's state-affiliated Mehr news agency called for a shift to a war economy and urged adopting psychological warfare tactics modeled on Nazi Germany.

Al Jazeera published details of Iran's three-phase proposal, including mutual non-attack commitments, gradual mine-clearing with U.S. assistance, international oversight, revised compensation wording, a 15-year enrichment freeze with subsequent resumption at civilian levels without dismantlement, and a regional security dialogue.
Iranian state-backed news outlets reported that Iran received a U.S. response through Pakistani mediators to its 14-point proposal, and that Iranian decision-makers are reviewing it.
Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei confirmed receipt of the U.S. view and stated that Iran's response will be announced after final deliberation.

An Iranian report indicated that a high-level meeting of Parliamentary Speaker Ghalibaf, the IRGC, the president, and Foreign Minister Araghchi focused entirely on war scenarios rather than diplomacy, signaling preparations for a potential second phase of conflict.

Iran's Deputy Parliament Speaker Hamidreza Haji-Babaei said the U.S. must accept the Islamic Republic's 'ten conditions' and that negotiations are no longer about solving a problem but about reaching an agreement with a power.
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei stated that the U.S. response, received through Pakistan, contains excessive and unreasonable demands, and that details remain under review.
Iran executed three men linked to the January protests.

items.title: 美国侧面：油价与战争成本正在倒逼政策选择
items.description: 美国国内也在承受中东战事外溢压力。WIRE 信息显示，油价高位运行、战争成本估算上升，同时白宫仍在听取新的对伊朗打击和地面行动选项。对华盛顿而言，军事压力、国内成本和外交回旋空间正在同时收紧。
items.rawSummary: The United States has terminated Iran hostilities but maintains diplomatic talks and rejected Iran's latest enriched uranium proposal, adding a hardline advocate to its negotiating team, while the conflict's economic toll drives gasoline to $4.43 per gallon and delays NATO arms shipments.
items.analysis: President Trump notified Congress that Iran hostilities have terminated, but left the door open to renewed strikes and recently rejected Tehran's enriched uranium proposal, describing the military situation favorably. Despite the rejection, US envoy Witkoff stated that diplomatic talks with Iran are continuing, and the administration has now added Nick Stewart, a proponent of aggressive sanctions and potential military force, to the negotiating team. The economic toll of the recent conflict persists: average gasoline prices hit $4.43 per gallon, up 61% since December and projected to add $90 billion annually in consumer costs, while war expenses strain missile stockpiles, delaying weapons deliveries to NATO allies. The Treasury General Account surged to about $1 trillion on spring tax receipts, briefly pushing federal debt below $39 trillion, but short-term borrowing is expected to accelerate. Domestically, Spirit Airlines ceased operations and filed for bankruptcy, prompting a federal relief plan, and other notable developments include a 25 percent tariff on EU autos, Chinese naval activity near the Philippines, stalled Taiwan defense funding, and over $8.6 billion in approved military sales to Middle Eastern partners.

keyPoints.point: White House press secretary said only the president knows where things stand with Iran and what he will do.
President Trump called Iran's call for civilians to gather near energy stations illegal.
The White House stated President Trump has been made aware of Pakistan's ceasefire proposal and a response will come.
Senator Lindsey Graham called for a congressional review process for any ceasefire or peace agreement with Iran.
The White House announced President Trump will discuss the possibility of the US leaving NATO with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte.
Israel excluded France from upcoming direct talks with Lebanon scheduled in Washington, citing French initiatives against Israeli operations and a lack of willingness to help disarm Hezbollah.
Iranian officials stated the US is continuing with irreconcilable demands in talks.
The U.S. State Department revoked the green cards of three Iranian nationals linked to the regime.
Lebanese President expressed hope that upcoming direct talks with Israel in Washington will result in a ceasefire.
A preparatory meeting between Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors, hosted by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, is scheduled at the State Department.
The first direct talks in decades between Israel and Lebanon commenced in Washington, hosted by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
U.S. Central Command reported that no ships have made it past the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports since it began in March.
The United States and Iran may hold a second round of negotiations this week amid the ongoing ceasefire.
The first direct talks between Israel and Lebanon in Washington ended after more than three hours, with both sides describing them as positive.
The U.S. Senate scheduled votes on asserting war powers regarding Iran and on blocking arms sales to Israel.
The White House announced it will hold a call with U.S. oil executives on Thursday.
U.S. President Trump announced a 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon, brokered following direct talks, beginning Thursday.
President Trump stated he will invite the leaders of Israel and Lebanon to the White House for their first meaningful talks since 1983.
Israeli media reported top officials are increasingly frustrated with the U.S. ceasefire approach, as the deal was announced before UN Security Council approval.
The White House is investigating the strange deaths and disappearances of ten scientists involved in military research for the U.S. government.
A shooting was reported near the Waterfront Metro station in Washington D.C.
A second round of direct talks between Israel and Lebanon is set to take place in Washington.
The U.S. delegation, including Vice President JD Vance, did not depart for scheduled peace talks with Iran in Pakistan.
U.S. oil prices surged above $90 per barrel following confirmation that the U.S. delegation had not departed for Iran talks.
Vice President JD Vance attended White House policy meetings on the stalled U.S.-Iran negotiations.
Israeli media reported it is unlikely the U.S. and Iran will find points of convergence to enable a long-term ceasefire.
An assessment revealed the U.S. military has heavily depleted key missile stockpiles during the recent war, creating a near-term strategic vulnerability.
The U.S. Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control announced updates to its sanctions list, adding Iranian-linked individuals and entities.
President Trump convened a high-level meeting with Vice President Vance, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, and Joint Chiefs Chair Gen. Dan Caine.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived at the White House alongside Secretary of War Pete Hegseth.
U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived at the White House.
U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee was recalled to Washington D.C.
The White House presented Congress with a record $1.5 trillion Pentagon budget request, a 42% increase focused on munitions and hardware.
The White House convened a meeting with Trump, Vance, Rubio, Hegseth, and Caine, settling on seeking a ceasefire extension with Iran.
President Trump publicly attacked the Wall Street Journal and defended his administration's record on Iran.
U.S. officials stated President Trump is offering Iran a limited 3-5 day window to respond with a clear negotiating position, describing it as a final opportunity.
The White House developed a list of NATO countries to potentially punish for refusing to back the Iran war.
U.S. Secretary of the Navy John C. Phelan was fired by the Pentagon, with Undersecretary Hung Cao assuming duties as acting Secretary.
The U.S. Senate blocked an Iran war powers resolution for the fifth consecutive time.
Reports indicated the firing of the Secretary of the Navy was linked to tensions over modernization, shipbuilding delays, and chain-of-command disputes.
President Trump stated he is not anxious to make a deal and all pressure is on Iran.
The U.S. accused China of industrial-scale theft of U.S. AI technology, warning it could raise tensions ahead of a planned summit.
DOJ detains U.S. Soldier accused of $400,000 bet on Maduro's removal.
Large plume of smoke visible near the U.S. Capitol building, bus fire reported.
Pentagon exploring options to punish NATO allies that did not support US operations against Iran.
In Washington, D.C., 20,000 teddy bears were displayed as part of a protest calling on Russia to return Ukrainian children.
DOJ announces arrest of 25 members and associates of the Mexican Mafia prison gang on federal indictments.
The US and EU signed a deal to cooperate on critical minerals.
Bus crash near the Pentagon injures 23, including 10 Department of War personnel.
Administration considers using the Defense Production Act to bail out Spirit Airlines, citing rising jet fuel costs from the Iran war.
Rep. Jim Jordan investigates ActBlue over suspected foreign donations.
New immigration guidance allows officials to deny green cards based on political views, including participation in pro-Palestinian protests.
Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu is expected to travel to Washington in mid-May for a potential summit with Lebanese President Michel Aoun.
Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao pledged to defend the homeland, support sailors, and build more ships.
Reports indicate FBI Director Kash Patel is increasingly expected to be removed.
President Trump was rushed off stage by Secret Service during the White House Correspondents' Dinner after shots were fired.
The suspected shooter was killed in the lobby of the White House Correspondents Dinner event.
Following evacuation, the dinner hosts announced the program would resume; Vice President Vance was confirmed uninjured.
President Trump released a statement following the shooting.
The assailant, armed with a long rifle and multiple magazines, attempted to charge through the magnetometer screening area and fired at Secret Service before being shot dead.
A law enforcement officer was shot in the chest but saved by a bulletproof vest.
Trump announced law enforcement requested the premises be vacated; a press conference was scheduled and the dinner would be rescheduled.
Conflicting reports emerged indicating the suspected shooter was alive and in custody, contradicting earlier information.
The shooter was identified as 31-year-old Cole Tomas Allen from Torrance, California.
A protester wearing a keffiyeh reportedly rushed the motorcade in Washington, D.C., and was arrested just before the White House Correspondents' Dinner shooting.
Mexican President Sheinbaum expressed relief that President Trump and his wife were safe.
The FBI confirmed the suspect is in custody and was armed with a shotgun and a handgun, contradicting earlier reports of a long rifle.
President Trump released CCTV footage of the attack and stated a Secret Service officer was saved by his bulletproof vest.
President Trump released a photo of the suspected shooter, Cole Tomas Allen.
Reports indicated the shooter was a supporter of former Vice President Kamala Harris.
At a press conference, President Trump stated the shooting would not deter him from winning the war in Iran and described the suspect as a 'whackjob' lone wolf.
President Trump stated he does not think the suspect can be linked to the situation in Iran.
President Trump declared the shooting will not deter the U.S. from winning the war in Iran.
D.C. Police Chief reported the suspect was armed with a hunting rifle, a pistol, and several knives.
The FBI's Joint Terrorism Task Force arrived at the shooting scene.
D.C. Mayor stated there is no reason to believe another person is involved in the incident.
D.C. Police Chief confirmed the suspected shooter was not struck by gunfire and is uninjured.
President Trump issued a statement asking all Americans to recommit to resolving their differences peacefully.
The suspect was charged with felony firearms and assault charges against a federal officer.
FBI Director Kash Patel stated the investigation will thoroughly examine the individual's background.
U.S. AAG Todd Blanche announced the suspect will appear in court tomorrow.
Indian Prime Minister Modi expressed relief and unequivocally condemned violence following the shooting.
The FBI arrived at the California home of the shooter to execute a search.
U.S. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche stated the suspect was determined to inflict the maximum amount of harm.
FBI SWAT personnel entered the California home of the suspected shooter.
The gunman confessed that he was targeting President Trump's officials.
Authorities obtained a warrant and breached the California home linked to the shooter.
The gunman clarified he intended to target Trump administration officials broadly, not specifically mentioning the president.
Polling and Senate vote results reveal a historic shift in U.S. public opinion, with greater popular support for Palestine than Israel.
US markets anticipate significant reaction to the cancellation of US-Iran talks, with oil prices surging.
The shooter's manifesto explicitly named Trump administration officials as targets and contained anti-Trump and anti-Christian content.
Discussions at the White House considered whether President Trump may need to wear a bulletproof vest at future public events.
The shooter was identified as having attended a 'No Kings' protest in California and was linked to a group called 'Wide Awake'.
Food inflation data shows a sharp acceleration, with average inflation for food and beverage companies surging 7.9% year-over-year in March.
President Trump is scheduled to appear on 60 Minutes to provide a detailed account of the previous night's shooting.
The shooter's manifesto outlined a plan to target Trump administration officials prioritized from highest-ranking to lowest, while specifically exempting FBI Director Kash Patel.

President Trump, speaking on 60 Minutes, revealed that he likely slowed Secret Service evacuation efforts during the shooting.
The White House Correspondents' Dinner was held with a lower level of security than typically used for events attended by top U.S. leaders.
President Trump slammed a CBS reporter as a 'DISGRACE' after she made reference to the term 'pedophile' from the shooter's manifesto.
A new bill (H.R. 8445) was introduced to extend U.S. legal protections to Americans serving in the Israeli army.
President Trump is convening top officials to discuss next steps on Iran amid the negotiation deadlock, including a potential resumption of the bombing campaign.
The sister of WHCD shooter Cole Tomas Allen revealed he was increasingly radical and hid firearms at their parents' Maryland home.
Vice President JD Vance privately raised doubts about the Pentagon's portrayal of U.S. weapons stockpile strength in the Iran war.
Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt stated that President Trump spoke with the wounded Secret Service agent following the shooting.

Investigators are probing the WHCD shooter's possible ties to Stacey Abrams' Fair Fight Action and Black Lives Matter.
President Trump's national security team is discussing Iran's latest proposal, which Iran had delivered to Pakistan three days ago.

King Charles III addressed the U.S. Congress during his state visit.

The Pentagon asked Congress to formally rename the Department of Defense to the 'Department of War'.
Former FBI Director James Comey was charged with threatening to harm President Trump in an Instagram post.
An arrest warrant was issued for former FBI Director James Comey.
A resolution to prevent President Trump from launching strikes on Cuba was rejected in the U.S. Senate.
President Trump and First Lady Melania Trump hosted King Charles III and Queen Camilla for the White House state dinner.
The Pentagon is considering outsourcing warship design and building to Korea and Japan, according to USNI News.
President Trump met with oil executives as gasoline prices rose to about $4.18 per gallon, according to Axios.
U.S. oil prices surged toward $105 per barrel ahead of earnings reports and a Federal Reserve rate decision.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth delivered opening remarks before the House Armed Services Committee on the requested $1.7 trillion defense budget.

The Supreme Court is weighing President Trump's authority to end migrant protections.
U.S. 10-year Treasury note yield rose above 4.40% while U.S. oil prices surged above $108 per barrel.

The Pentagon's comptroller told the House Armed Services Committee that the current estimated cost of the Iran War is $25 billion.
Axios reported that President Trump is slated to receive a briefing from CENTCOM Commander Adm. Brad Cooper on new military options against Iran.
U.S. oil prices surged above $109 per barrel, a 28% increase in eight trading days.
Retired Admiral William McRaven expressed concern that recent Pentagon leadership dismissals may cause senior officers to fear speaking truth to power.
King Charles III and Queen Camilla arrived at the White House for a formal farewell hosted by President Trump and the First Lady.
A deadline nears for President Trump to either end the Iran war or present a case to Congress for its extension.
The U.S. Senate banned senators from trading on prediction markets.
The U.S. House passed a DHS funding bill, sending it to President Trump.
The DHS shutdown, which began in February, is set to end after the House passed a funding bill covering most of the agency, including TSA.
The White House stated that 'Mythos' is not a doomsday device.

President Trump called for terminating the Senate filibuster to pass the Save America Act.
President Trump invited the newly elected Iraqi Prime Minister to Washington D.C.
The U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia released footage showing Cole Allen shooting a Secret Service officer during the attempted assassination.

U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro released footage showing Cole Allen rushing past security at the White House Correspondents' Dinner.

U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro released additional security footage showing Cole Allen walking through the Hilton Hotel the day before the shooting.

Taiwan's special defense budget remains stalled due to partisan gridlock, despite increased U.S. pressure to pass it, with divisions within the KMT further complicating efforts.
